cards.explanation: The answer is False. Solomon, David's son and Israel's king (Proverbs 1:1), says whoever is led astray by wine and strong drink “…is not wise.” Wine is called a mocker and strong drink a brawler. Anyone led astray by them is not wise, friends.

The answer is that he forfeits his own life. The king's terror is compared to a lion's roar, and the verse says whoever provokes him forfeits his own life. So this isn't a small thing to stir up. Poking a lion is just not a plan, friends.

The word is honorable. Solomon says it is honorable for a man to resolve a dispute. Then he adds that any fool will quarrel, which is the easy road. Ending an argument takes more strength than starting one.
The answer is nothing. At harvest time the slacker looks, but nothing is there. He skipped the plowing in season, so he has nothing to gather. Seeds don't plant themselves, friends.

The answer is a man of understanding. The intentions of a man's heart are deep waters, and the verse says it's the man of understanding who draws them out. Deep water, friends, and he's the one who gets the bucket all the way down.
The answer is a trustworthy man. Many a man proclaims his loving devotion, but who can find a trustworthy one? Words are cheap, friends. A trustworthy man is the rare one.
The answer is True. The righteous man walks with integrity, and the verse says blessed are his children after him. How he lives reaches past himself. His kids are in on the blessing.

The question points to this answer: no one can truly say it. Solomon asks who can say, “I have kept my heart pure; I am cleansed from my sin…” and he doesn't name a single volunteer. The question just hangs there while nobody steps forward. I think that's his point, friends.
The word is detestable. Differing weights and unequal measures are both detestable to the LORD. Cheating on the scale isn't a tiny thing to Him. He cares about honest dealing, friends.
The word is actions. Even a young man is known by his actions, by whether his conduct is pure and upright. You can see who someone is by what they do. Age doesn't change that.
The word is sleep. Do not love sleep, or you will grow poor. Then the verse says open your eyes, and you will have plenty of food. A pillow is a lovely thing, friends, but it won't pay the bills.

The answer is that he gloats. The buyer says “Worthless, worthless!” and then on the way out, he gloats. Sounds like the goods weren't so worthless after all. I think he likes his deal a little too much.

The answer is True. There is an abundance of gold and rubies, but lips of knowledge are a rare treasure. Gold and rubies come in abundance in this verse. Lips of knowledge are the rare treasure, friends.

The word is gravel. Food gained by fraud is sweet to a man, but later his mouth is full of gravel. The sweetness doesn't last, and the crunch comes after. Ouch, friends, my teeth hurt just reading it.
The answer is by consultation. Solomon says to set plans by consultation, which means asking others and not just going it alone. Plans get better when more than one head is in the kitchen, friends.

The answer is True. Right alongside setting plans by consultation, Solomon says to wage war under sound guidance. Both lines sit together in the same verse. Even the biggest, riskiest plans need good counsel behind them.

The word is avoid. The verse says he who reveals secrets is a constant gossip, so avoid the one who babbles with his lips. If someone can't keep a secret, they're not the one to hand yours to. Simple enough to remember, friends.

The answer is that it goes out in deepest darkness. Whoever curses his father or mother, his lamp will be extinguished in deepest darkness. It's a heavy one, so I'm saying it plainly. Honoring parents matters, friends.

The answer is False. Solomon says an inheritance gained quickly will not be blessed in the end. The verse points to no blessing at the end, so getting it fast doesn't come out well. Quick isn't the same as blessed, friends.
The answer is to wait on the LORD. Solomon says not to say, “I will avenge this evil!” and tells us to wait on the LORD, and He will save you. Handing it to Him is the way out, friends.

The answer is True. Solomon says unequal weights are detestable to the LORD, and dishonest scales are no good. Weights came up earlier, in Proverbs 20:10. He's coming back to the same point, so I think it matters.

The answer is False. Solomon says a man's steps are from the LORD, and then asks how anyone can understand his own way. The question leans toward no. Our steps come from the LORD, and that's more than we can map out ourselves, friends.

The answer is dedicating something rashly and reconsidering later. It is a trap for a man to dedicate something rashly, only later to reconsider his vows. The trap is the rash dedicating and the reconsidering that comes after. Think first, promise second, friends.

The answer is that it searches out his inmost being. The spirit of a man is the lamp of the LORD, searching out his inmost being. It's a light that looks deep inside. The lamp belongs to the LORD, friends, and it's the spirit of a man.

The answer is loving devotion and faithfulness. Those preserve a king, and by these he maintains his throne. Those are the two Solomon names. Character is what holds the throne in this verse, friends.

The words are strength and gray. The glory of young men is their strength, and gray hair is the splendor of the old. Those silver strands are called splendor here, friends, not something to hide. That's the whole saying, one half for the young and one half for the old.

The word is cleanse. Solomon says lashes and wounds scour evil, and beatings cleanse the inmost parts. This is a heavy one, so I'll just stick to what the verse says. The word it uses is cleanse, friends.
